messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@cloudbridge.com>

Subject: Feature request: per-route cost + latency dashboards for CloudBridge

Hi team,

Quick one from CloudBridge (cc Ellen). They want a console view that lets their SREs and FinOps slice cost and latency by route/endpoint. High-level asks:

- Per-route P50/P95 latency (filterable by model version, region, timeframe)
- Cost breakdown by route (tokens used, embeddings, inference compute) and ability to export CSV for chargeback
- Drill-down to see most expensive users / routes over a chosen period
- Saved dashboard views + a linkable view to include in their weekly ops report

They attached examples of what they use today (CloudBridge_console_examples.pdf) and a small sample of recent billing/call data (cost_samples.csv). They say this is a blocker to their quarterly expansion decision — if we can show a workable MVP they may commit to a larger Dedicated deal.

Can product/console assess feasibility and give a rough ETA (weeks) and minimal scope for an MVP? Also flag any data/ops constraints (cardinality, retention) we should surface to the customer.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Feature request: per-route cost + latency dashboards for CloudBridge

Thanks — good request. A few clarifying questions before I scope:

1) Real-time needs: does CloudBridge need live (sub-1m) updates or are 5–15 minute rollups acceptable?
2) Cost accuracy: are estimated cost figures OK for the MVP or do they require exact per-invoice matching?
3) Cardinality: roughly how many routes/endpoints do they expect to surface (dozens vs thousands)?

Quick thoughts on approach:
- Add a route_id tag to requests at the proxy/router level (low risk)
- Emit lightweight telemetry with token_count_estimate + model_id + route_id per request (sampling possible)
- Backend: aggregate into time-bucketed tables, surface P50/P95 latency and cost estimate panel per route
- Console: saved views and CSV export (low UI complexity)

Tradeoffs: exact per-request billing is expensive if we need to account for batching/caching precisely. We can deliver useful cost signals with sampled token estimates and an attribution model that adjusts for batching.

If this sounds reasonable I’ll draft an MVP scope and rough ETA (story points). Suggest a 30-min sync with CloudBridge and Eng this week.

-marcus
Marcus Lin

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature request: per-route cost + latency dashboards for CloudBridge

High level: doable, but several engineering/ops considerations.

Notes:
- Batching & caching: per-request token attribution is fuzzy because of runtime batching and KV/prefix cache hits. We can estimate token count per-request but will need correction factors for shared batches and cache hits.
- Telemetry: we need route_id + model_version + sampling flag emitted at the router. That requires a small change in the request path (non-invasive).
- Storage & retention: per-route, per-version metrics increase cardinality. We should implement pre-aggregation (route hash -> time bucket) and a 90/365 day retention policy for aggregated metrics.

Proposal for MVP (minimal to ship in 6–8 weeks):
- Backend: aggregation job that computes P50/P95 latency and token_count_estimate per route per 5-min bucket
- Console: per-route dashboard with filter by model_version/region, CSV export, and a saved view mechanism
- Billing: attach an "estimated cost" column using token cost heuristics (not invoice-grade)

Estimated effort: ~3 engineering sprints (1 backend lead + 1 infra + 1 frontend). To proceed we need two infra exceptions:
1) Temporary higher metrics ingestion quota for CloudBridge (to collect route-tag telemetry during beta)
2) Permission to add route_id to telemetry (requires Product sign-off)

Tech notes attached and a drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/console-observability-notes (see tech-notes.md).

If Product confirms prioritization, Eng can draft a more precise plan + acceptance criteria.

-Stephanie

Subject: Re: Feature request: per-route cost + latency dashboards for CloudBridge

Ops note: cardinality is the main risk. If route_id is an arbitrary free text from the customer we risk high metric cardinality and Prometheus blowup. Recommendations:

- Force route_id to a hashed namespace (route_hash) and limit distinct values per account to a configurable limit (e.g., 200)
- Pre-aggregate to 5-min buckets and store in time-series store optimized for pre-aggregates
- For the beta, whitelist CloudBridge for a temporary ingestion increase (Jira SUP-3921) so we don't drop telemetry during testing

I’ll file the ops change and can prepare the ingestion whitelist if Product approves.

-Rishi
